match.reason: The closest bank point, chem-ionic-bonding, is written at Year 11 depth, covering lattices, melting points and conduction, and it does not teach the Stage 5 idea of atoms gaining or losing electrons to reach a full outer shell, so it is a different depth rather than a small adaptation.

draft.title: Ions and ionic bonding
card: Atoms are most stable when their outer shell is full. Many atoms reach this by gaining or losing electrons.
an atom that has gained or lost electrons, so it has an electric charge. Losing electrons makes a positive ion. Gaining electrons makes a negative ion.
the attraction between positive and negative ions. It forms when a metal gives electrons to a non-metal.
Sodium has one outer electron and chlorine has seven. Sodium gives one to chlorine, so sodium becomes Na\u207a and chlorine becomes Cl\u207b. They attract to form sodium chloride (NaCl).
draft.remember: Metals lose electrons and non-metals gain them. Opposite charges attract to form an ionic bond.

a.q: A magnesium atom loses two electrons. What does it become?
opts: A neutral atom with a full shell
a.why: Losing negative electrons leaves more protons than electrons, so the atom becomes a positive ion. A negative ion forms when electrons are gained, not lost.
a.clue: Electrons carry a negative charge. What is left when some go?

b.q: Which statement best describes the ionic bond in sodium chloride?
opts: Positive sodium ions attract negative chloride ions
Sodium and chlorine atoms share a pair of electrons
Sodium atoms gain an electron from chlorine atoms
Negative sodium ions attract positive chloride ions
b.why: Sodium gives an electron to chlorine, so sodium forms a positive ion and chlorine a negative ion, and they attract. The option with the charges swapped is tempting, but metals lose electrons so they form positive ions.
b.clue: Which atom loses an electron, and what charge does that give it?

b.best: Positive sodium ions attract negative chloride ions
